input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Run comparison view for training and pipeline runs

## Description

Delivers a run-comparison surface in the Dashboard: users select two or more training or pipeline runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side, with a diff presentation over the same surface that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. This is the P0 core of the strategy and delivers independent user value (comparison today happens in exported spreadsheets).

## Scope

- Multi-selection of two or more runs from the existing runs list in the Dashboard, covering both training runs and pipeline runs.
- Side-by-side rendering of the selected runs' parameters and metrics.
- A diff presentation over the same comparison surface that highlights which parameters and metrics differ between two selected runs (the strategy's "diff view" is a presentation mode of the side-by-side comparison over the same run data — one surface, two modes).
- The comparison reads run parameters and metrics through the same data sources that back the existing per-run Dashboard pages (no new data plane).
- Data Science Pipelines is a passive component in this strategy: no code changes there; the existing KFP v2 run surfaces continue to serve run data. Validation of that passive classification is an acceptance criterion below.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given two or more runs selected from the runs list, When the user opens the comparison, Then all selected runs' parameters and metrics render side by side in the Dashboard.
- Given two runs in the comparison, When the user switches to the diff presentation, Then the parameters and metrics that changed between the two runs are highlighted.
- Given a mix of training runs and pipeline runs, When compared, Then both run kinds are selectable and their parameters and metrics render correctly in the comparison (this validates the passive Data Science Pipelines component — no Data Science Pipelines code changes are required for the comparison to work).
- The comparison is reachable without leaving the project context of the selected runs.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard — fully covered by this epic.
- **HLR-3 (P1, bundled with HLR-1)**: The run "diff" view is a presentation mode of the same comparison surface over the same run data (same component, same team, same data structure); covering both in one epic avoids building the same surface twice. Covered at the epic's P0 priority.

# Run linkage on registered model versions

## Description

Registered model versions in the Model Registry record a resolvable link back to the run (training or pipeline run) that produced them, and that linkage is exposed through the registry's existing entity and REST API surfaces so platform consumers — including the Dashboard's registry experience — can resolve a model version to its originating run. This epic delivers the registry side of the model-version-to-run linkage; the Dashboard-side entry point that consumes it is a separate epic owned by the Dashboard team.

## Scope

- Support recording the originating run on a registered model version using the registry's documented model-version metadata extension point (custom properties on ModelVersion entities) or an equivalent supported mechanism — the specific mechanism is an implementation decision for the Model Registry team.
- Expose the run linkage through the registry's OpenAPI-specified REST API so consumers can read the originating run for a given model version.
- Ensure model versions registered from runs in the platform carry the linkage (population at registration time, whether via registration flows or client SDK usage).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a model version registered from a run in the platform, When the version is read via the registry REST API, Then the originating run is resolvable from the version's metadata.
- Given a model version with no known originating run, When read via the API, Then the linkage is absent or empty without errors (backward compatible with existing model versions).
- The linkage mechanism is documented in the registry's API surface (OpenAPI) so downstream consumers can build against it.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P1, registry side)**: "Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them" — the data/API half of this requirement is covered by this epic; the "so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry" (UI) half is covered by the Dashboard registry-experience epic.

# Open run comparisons from the Model Registry

## Description

In the Dashboard's registry experience, a registered model version surfaces the run that produced it, and the user can open a run comparison from there. This epic consumes two capabilities delivered elsewhere in the strategy: the run-comparison surface in the Dashboard (side-by-side and diff views over selected runs) and the run-linkage data recorded on registered model versions by the Model Registry. It depends on both — the entry point opens the comparison surface and reads the version's run linkage.

## Scope

- In the registry UI (model version view), surface the originating run recorded on the model version.
- Provide an action to open the run comparison for the linked run, landing in the run-comparison capability with the linked run selected so further runs can be added for side-by-side or diff comparison.
- Keep the registry-originated comparison consistent with the runs-list-originated comparison (same surface, same data rendering).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version with a recorded originating run, When the user views the version in the registry UI, Then the originating run is shown and an action to open its comparison is available.
- Given the user invokes that action, When the comparison opens, Then it is populated with the linked run and ready for side-by-side and diff comparison against other runs.
- Given a model version with no recorded originating run, When viewed in the registry UI, Then the version renders normally with the comparison action absent or disabled (no errors).
- The registry-originated comparison renders parameters and metrics identically to the runs-list-originated comparison.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P1, UI side)**: "so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry" — the user-facing half of the requirement, covered by this epic on top of the registry-side run linkage.

# Document the run comparison workflow

## Description

Product documentation covering the run-comparison workflow from both entry points named in the strategy: the runs list and the Model Registry. Written through the Red Hat docs content process after the implemented behavior exists, and technically reviewed against it.

## Scope

Content outline (authored inside the docs content process):

- **Comparison from the runs list**: selecting two or more training or pipeline runs, the side-by-side parameters/metrics view, and the diff presentation highlighting what changed between two runs.
- **Comparison from the Model Registry**: the run linkage on registered model versions and opening a comparison from a model version.
- **Boundaries**: what comparison does not do — no automatic best-run selection or promotion, no comparison across clusters or across projects (per the strategy's out-of-scope list).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A published documentation topic covers the comparison workflow from the runs list, including multi-run selection, the side-by-side view, and the diff view, for both training and pipeline runs.
- A published documentation topic covers opening a comparison from the Model Registry via a model version's run linkage.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented comparison behavior (runs-list and registry entry points) and any discrepancies found during review are resolved.
- The documented workflow matches the shipped behavior for the out-of-scope boundaries (no cross-cluster/cross-project comparison, no automatic selection).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)**: "Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry" — fully covered by this epic.
